newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisian dinar set for calm year - banker.
newsitem.headline: Tunisian dinar set for calm year - banker.

text.p: The Tunisian dinar is set for a "calm" year on the foreign exchange market in 1997 given reassuring economic indicators, Hatem Zaara, the head of Amen Bank's dealing department told the bank's annual forex meeting on Tuesday.
"Today, and given the reassuring economic indicators, we can affirm that the dinar will have a new calm year," he said.

Zaara said the forecast was based on the fall in the annual inflation rate to 3.7 percent in 1996 from 6.3 percent in 1995, the rise of exports which represented 30 percent of the gross domestic product (GDP), and steady consumption which grew by 4.1 percent in real terms.
Zaara said he expected higher foreign investment inflows in 1997 after the government decided that foreign investors would be free to purchase up to 49 percent of the capital of Tunisian firms.
"The dinar's bahavior in regard to the (recent) exponential rise of the U.S. currency had been marked by an astonishing calm," he said.
The dollar hit a record 1.0925 dinars on the Tunisian domestic market on March 7, reflecting the dollar's overall strength on international markets. The dollar was 1.0720/10 dinars on Tuesday.

Houssein Mouelhi, Director of Amen Bank's International Department, said that in coming years Tunisia will need to keep its economic indicators as close as possible to the performance of European Union countries when they establish the single European currency.
"The Tunisian dinar is very strongly linked to the European currencies because Tunisia's foreign trade with the EU countries represent some 80 percent of the total," Mouelhi said.
"The first objective for Tunisia is to have indicators close to the criteria to be met by any European country under the Maastricht requirements," he added.

Mouelhi said that in the long term the Euro will represent a reduction of foreign exchange risks because Tunisia, which in signed a free trade accord with the EU in 1995, will have to deal with only one European currency and not 15.
